questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Pull someone's leg
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

The idiom “pull someone’s leg” means “deceive someone playfully; tease someone.”

In a sentence: I think he was just **pulling your leg** when he said you've failed in the exam. 

The phrase first appeared in the late 1800s in America. The origin is not clear, though there are two popular theories, but both implausible. The first theory says that thieves used to pull the legs of their victims to put them off guard so that they could rob them. The second one refers to hangings that were held in Tyburn, England. It is said that people were hired to hang on the victim's leg to give them a quick execution. 

The rest of the options are incorrect.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required,bselect No improvement.**

She __read that novel __since she got up in the morning.
questions.solution:
The underlined part of the sentence is incorrect and has to be improved.

It should be replaced with “has been reading that novel”. This is in the present perfect continuous tense.

The present perfect continuous tense (also known as the present perfect progressive tense) shows that something started in the past and is continuing at the present time. The present perfect continuous is formed using the construction **has/have been + the present participle (root + -ing)**.

Eg: I have been reading War and Peace for a month now.

The rest of the options makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:

PARDON
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Pardon means “release (an offender) from the legal consequences of an offense or conviction, and often implicitly from blame.” The word that is an antonym of this is “Punish: inflict a penalty or sanction on (someone) as retribution for an offense, especially a transgression of a legal or moral code.”

**Grace**: courteous goodwill.

**Mercy**: compassion or forgiveness shown towards someone whom it is within one's power to punish or harm.

Options 1, 2 and 3 are nouns and are not antonyms of the verb “pardon”.

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

The crop was adversely affected by the inadequate rainfall.

options.text: The inadequate rainfall was adversely affecting the crop.
The adversely rainfall has affected the inadequate crop.
The inadequate crop adversely affected the rainfall.
The inadequate rainfall adversely affected the crop.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The inadequate rainfall adversely affected the crop.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in a passive voice form, hence we need to convert it into an active voice form.
 
 
• Find the subject (The crop) and object (the inadequate rainfall. ) of the sentence and exchange their places. 
 
• The given sentence is in the simple past tense. The active verb form for simple past is: 
 
 
• Subject + V2 + object.
 
 
 
• So, 'was adversely affected' changes to adversely affected'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part. 

**Following these steps, we finally get-** The inadequate rainfall adversely affected the crop.​

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.solution:
The word to be used in the blank is “largest”.

The superlative(the third or highest degree of comparison in adjectives or adverbs) of “large”, which is “largest” has to be used here since the word preceding the blank is “world’s”. This indicates that when considering all the water bodies on this earth, the Pacific Ocean covers a vast area. 

“Larger” is a comparative(the second or middle degree of comparison in adjectives or adverbs).

The comparative and superlative degrees are formed by adding the -er and -est suffix to adjectives and adverbs with a single consonant for an ending.

Comparative adjectives are used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher). They are used in sentences where two nouns are compared, in this pattern:

Noun (subject) + verb + comparative adjective + than + noun (object).

**Superlative adjectives are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest). They are used in sentences where a subject is compared to a group of objects.**

Noun (subject) + verb + the + superlative adjective + noun (object).

“Large” means “of considerable or relatively great size, extent, or capacity” and “more large” is grammatically incorrect, both these options are cancelled.

Hence the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
**Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.**

A person who draws or produces maps
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2. 

A cartographer is a person that makes maps.

Up until the 18th century, maps were often decorated with fanciful beasts and monsters, at the expense of accurate details about places. French mapmakers of the 1700s and 1800s encouraged the use of more scientific methods in the art they called "cartographie." The French word ***cartographie*** (the science of making maps), from which we get our English word "cartography," was created from "carte," meaning "*map*," and "-*graphie*," meaning "representation by." Around the same time, we adopted "cartography" in the mid-19th century, we also created our word for a mapmaker, "cartographer.”

The rest of the options are incorrect as:

A **choreographer **is a person who composes the sequence of steps and moves for a performance of dance.

A **lexicographer** is a person who compiles dictionaries.

A **calligrapher** is one who practices calligraphy. It is the art of producing decorative handwriting or lettering with a pen or brush.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. And 844 million don’t have access to clean water close to home, according to the latest report by WaterAid.

B. Around 4 billion people in the world live in physically water-scarce areas.

C. It is because globally we use six times as much water today as we did 100 years ago.

D. The world’s water crisis is getting worse.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4: BADC**

We can gather from the above sentences that the paragraph is about the global water crisis. 

Sentence **B** comes 1st as a paragraph always starts with a general statement and B serves as the introductory sentence of the para which introduces us to the topic. 

Sentence **A** comes 2nd as it sheds more light on the issue mentioned in sentence B.

Sentence **D **follows A as it gives us a gist of the topic mentioned in sentences B and A.

Sentence **C** follows B as it provides a reason for the water crisis getting worse- an issue mentioned in sentence D.

*Hence the correct order is BADC*.

questions.question:

A. An estimated 70% of this plastic enters the sea sinks

B. This is a problem that stretches far beyond India

C. Eight million tonnes of plastic ends up in the world 's oceans every year, causing damage to the fragile ecosystem

D. And much of it is not biodegradable
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2: CADB.**

We can gather from the above sentences that the paragraph is about the non-biodegradable plastic found in the water bodies.

Sentence C is 1st as all paragraphs should start with a general statement which introduces a new topic.

Sentence A is 2nd as "this plastic" refers to the plastic mentioned in sentence C. 

Sentence D is 3rd as it starts with "and" which is adding more information to sentence D.

Sentence B is 4th as the problem mentioned here is the plastic ending up in sea sinks.
